explanation: Fires on verbs and function words inside infinitive or complement clauses in prose ('need to[[ force]]', 'intended to[[ impose]]', 'as if it[[ never]]', 'I[[ want]]'), often where a word about imposing or creating comes next. The cue is mostly the clause structure before the token, not the token's identity. Weak on ordinary nouns and punctuation.

Fires on many kinds of mid-sentence content tokens in expository and news prose (adverbs, verbs, adjectives, word-piece continuations such as 'spec|ulating', 'unce|asing') with no shared lexical theme. It looks like a diffuse prose-continuation feature, with no clear trigger.

Fires inside high-entropy, structured identifier strings: GUID hyphens, digits in IDs, timestamps and URLs, URL short-codes, format placeholders like {4}, list-separator quotes, and whitespace runs in code or markup. The context (random alphanumeric or machine-formatted text) matters more than the token itself. Plain prose gives little or nothing.

Fires on items and separators in enumerated lists: the next element or the comma/'and'/'&' in a series ('ONE: "one",[[ TWO]]', 'AL','AK','AZ[[',']]', 'Personal Care[[ and]]', countdown digits, sequential D3). It fires most strongly in code literals of enumerations, and moderately on 'and' joining paired nouns in prose.

Fires on a function word or modifier right after a verb or noun, where it introduces a complement or a superlative/evaluative phrase: 'do it[[ for]] money', 'one of the[[ leading]] causes', 'UK's[[ oldest]]', 'drugs[[ of]] abuse', 'with[[ poor]] prognosis'. It is strongest in biomedical-abstract phrasing like 'one of the leading causes of', and also on casual 'for' + duration. The trigger is context-driven and mixed.

Fires on the second or later word-piece of non-English (mostly South Asian, Turkic or Arabic) proper names and place names split into subwords: 'Ali[[ As]]ghar', 'B[[ih]]ari', 'South W[[az]]iristan', 'Gur|udaspur', 'Saravan Pan[[th]]am'. Smaller offshoots: format strings in code ('%Y') and rare technical terms. Common English words give little.

Fires on digits inside citation or reference IDs (e.g. '@B1-ijerph-17-0[[1]]067', DOI digits). It also fires on a scattered set of tokens that complete a fixed compound or term, such as 'cheated[[ on]]', 'system[[ path]]', 'back[[cross]]' and 'years[[ old]]'. Main job: digits in bibliographic reference codes; the rest is mixed.

Fires on the first token of a new paragraph after a blank line (double newline), especially when it follows a title or heading or ends a code block: 'It', 'I', 'The', 'Our', 'All', or Cyrillic 'В'. The token's position at the start of body text is what matters. Sentence-initial words with no preceding blank line give weak activation.

Fires on the head or second part of compound technical modifiers that describe a product's design type or spec: 'dual[[ reel]]', 'cylindrical-b[[ore]]', 'Oetiker[[-style]]', 'high[[-performance]]', 'twin[[-site]]', '12,000[[ capacity]]', 'high[[ quality]]', 'multi-ch[[amber]]'. Typically it is the noun or suffix after an adjective, number or hyphen in a classifying compound.

Fires on boundary tokens that end one segment before new content starts, such as the end of an XML declaration '"?>\n', a closing quote plus newline in require lines, a colon plus newline after a question, and 'and[[/or]]'. It also fires on 'about[[ to]]', 'stand[[ to]]', 'Thanks in[[ advance]]' and some name word-pieces. The examples are a mixture without one clear rule.

Fires on the first word-piece of a capitalized word split into subwords, usually after a space: 'Ind|us', 'Ind|ividually', 'Th|ematic', 'Sh|aukat', 'Sh|aving', 'Sp|okes', 'St|igmatisation'. Common onsets like Sh, Ind, Th, St and Sp are the strongest. Whole capitalized words that are not split, like 'The', give weak activation.

Fires on the last token of a noun phrase that names the topic being introduced, often right after 'a', 'the' or 'this': 'a[[ method]]', 'This[[ boot]]', 'a sql[[ query]]', the year-range end digit in '1968–6[[9]] Oakland Seals season', and completions of technical terms ('hyperbar[[ic]]', 'cyclosp[[or]]in'). It is common in technical Q&A and patents. Moderately coherent.

Fires on the main verb (or modal/'able') that comes right after the subject of a clause, in narrative or informal prose: 'you'll be[[ able]]', 'if they[[ find]]', 'Things[[ got]]', 'there[[ exists]]', 'I[[ get]]', 'the problem[[ went]] away', 'you[[ can]] see'. The trigger is the predicate position after a subject.

Fires on the second token of fixed multi-token names and stock phrases: 'PL/[[SQL]]', 'using namespace[[ std]]', 'source[[ code]]' (license boilerplate), 'OS[[ X]]', 'Crypto.Public[[Key]]', 'at the[[ very]] least', 'commercial[[ use]]'. The token is highly predictable from the token(s) before it.

Fires on words about physically mixing or agitating materials: 'stirring', 'shake', 'mixed', 'mixing', 'mechanically' scraped, 'emulsifying', 'mixture'. It is weaker on nearby tokens in chemistry or cooking text that describes combining substances.

Fires on the second token of compound technical names or abbreviations, especially names of assessment instruments ('Brief Symptom[[ Inventory]]', 'Anger[[ Scale]]', 'rating[[ scale]]'), legal reporter abbreviations ('N.J.[[ Super]].', 'Ill.[[ App]]', 'Cal[[.App]]'), the digits of error codes ('CS[[0]]246') and PHP 'protected[[ $]]'. These are mixed domains that share a 'continuation of a fixed technical name' pattern.

Fires on the preposition, comma or article that links a place to its larger administrative region in gazetteer-style location descriptions: 'district[[ of]] Gmina', 'capital city[[ of]]', 'Miri Division[[,]] Sarawak', 'in[[ the]] Swiss canton', 'located[[ in]]', 'immigrants[[ from]]'. It is weaker on similar connectives in other text.

Fires on 'WordPress' and its pieces ('wp', 'wordpress', 'Word Press', 'press'), and also on the 'O' in the patent code 'WO' and on W-prefixed codes ('W3', 'WO3', 'W1T'). In short: W-initial brand names or codes, centered on WordPress.

Fires on many content and function tokens with no shared theme: political party or person names (Labour, Biden, liberal), medical terms (implantation, intrauterine), 'episode[[ of]]', 'assist[[ from]]', 'Monday-F[[riday]]'. No consistent trigger is visible.

Fires on particles and prepositions that complete phrasal verbs of motion or continuation: 'keeps[[ on]]', 'come[[ out]]', 'passing[[ through]]', 'falls[[ below]]', 'passing[[ over]]', 'walked[[ towards]]', 'takes[[ on]]'. A separate offshoot fires on whitespace or indentation and ':=' in code.

Fires on markup symbols in scientific-article citation and anchor syntax: the '#' in 'Introduction {#sec1}', the '@' in '[@B1]', 'CR' in '[@CR2]', and 'ref-type'. It is weaker on '$' before amounts and on 'Pat.' periods.
